title: Parent board resolution
question: Why does our parent company sign a board resolution?

body.normal: When an existing company sets up an Indian subsidiary, its board formally approves the investment and names who will act for it. Your project lead drafts the resolution; the parent's board signs it and you upload the signed copy.
body.simple: Your parent company's board signs a paper approving the new Indian company.
body.detail: A company can only act through decisions of its board. The board resolution records that the parent approves forming the Indian company, subscribing to its shares and appointing an authorised representative to sign documents. Your project lead prepares the draft from the details you gave. The parent's directors sign it, and for a foreign parent it is often notarised or apostilled before it is used in the filing.
body.why: The Registrar relies on this resolution as proof that the parent really agreed to invest, so the filing cannot go ahead without it.

citations.label: Companies Act 2013, section 179 (powers of the board)
